selectedDefects.issueTitle: Mobile: Back button handler breaks after deleting the Welcome notebook and then going to settings
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the mobile app's own navigation history lives in a Redux reducer in packages/app-mobile/utils/appReducer.ts. Deleting the current notebook removed the last history entry without pushing a replacement, so the history could empty out and the hardware back button stopped working. The fix pushes DEFAULT_ROUTE when the history would otherwise be empty. This is the defining shape of a React Native defect: the bug is pure JavaScript running on Hermes, but the trigger is a native Android event, KEYCODE_BACK delivered by UiAutomator2, and the observation is the native view hierarchy that the JS side drives. Neither half alone reproduces it, which is exactly what the react-native-android adapter has to bridge
remaining: build the profileable variant at both revisions so the artifact is signed with the committed debug keystore
reset the AVD so the Welcome notebook exists, since the trigger depends on first-run content
author the trigger through UiAutomator2: delete the Welcome notebook, open settings, send KEYCODE_BACK, and read the resulting screen
state identity and authority: the platform back gesture must leave a screen the user navigated into
minimize the trigger and verify neighboring legal behavior: back from settings works on both builds when no notebook was deleted
prove three clean affected reproductions and three reached-observation fixed controls
selectedDefects.executionOutcome: complete campaign. Three affected reproductions all landing on react-native-navigation:hardware-back-exits-app-after-deleted-notebook, three fixed controls all reaching the same observation and returning to the note list, neighbouring legal behaviour holding on both revisions, and a passing cleanup audit. The affected build does not strand the user on settings as this record originally said: it leaves the application, because the emptied navigation history means nothing claims the back event

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Mobile: The manage profiles screen is not scrollable to the bottom entry
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the profile FlatList was wrapped in a plain View with no flex, so the native scroll container was measured to its natural height and the last profile could never be reached. The fix gives the list flex 1 and adds bottom content padding. The defect lives in a JavaScript style object, but it only becomes observable after the JS shadow tree is laid out and handed to the native Android view system, so the trigger is a UiAutomator2 scroll gesture and the observation is whether the last row becomes visible. It is the layout and measurement path of the adapter, distinct from the reducer and navigation path of the other joplin selection
remaining: build the profileable variant at both revisions
seed enough profiles that the list overflows the screen on the chosen AVD, and pin the AVD's screen size and density in the bounds since overflow depends on them
author the trigger: open settings, open manage profiles, scroll to the end, and assert the last entry is reachable
state identity and authority: a scrollable list must be able to reveal its last item
minimize the trigger and verify neighboring legal behavior: a list short enough to fit renders identically on both builds
prove three clean affected reproductions and three reached-observation fixed controls

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Mobile: There is a gap when side menus are opened in landscape mode
selectedDefects.whySuitable: SideMenu applied safe-area insets to the menu itself as padding, which in landscape left a visible gap between the menu and the screen edge on devices with cutouts. The fix removes the inset padding from the menu styles and restructures where the menu is mounted in root.tsx. The trigger needs a real device orientation change and real window insets, so it cannot be reproduced off-device: it exercises the adapter across an Android configuration change while the React Native surface re-measures. The observation is geometric, the bounds of the menu node relative to the display, which is a UiAutomator2 property rather than a semantics label
remaining: build the profileable variant at both revisions
choose an AVD whose insets actually reproduce the gap and record the exact device profile, since the upstream issue says on some devices
author the trigger: rotate to landscape, open the side menu, read the node bounds
state identity and authority for the geometry claim, and decide the tolerance before executing
minimize the trigger and verify neighboring legal behavior: the same menu in portrait is flush on both builds
prove three clean affected reproductions and three reached-observation fixed controls, and drop this candidate if no available AVD profile reproduces the inset condition

selectedDefects.issueTitle: X-ing a Notebook from "linked notebook" doesn't unlink notes from this Notebook
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the link-notebooks screen saved only the notebooks present in the selection store, so in single-select mode a notebook the user removed was never marked deselected and the note stayed linked. The fix diffs the initial selection against the current one and writes an explicit deselected state. This is a second, independent application whose defect class is persisted-state divergence rather than layout or navigation, and its observation is a database-backed list re-read after leaving and re-entering the screen, so the adapter has to hold an observation across a screen transition rather than within one render
remaining: build the release variant at both revisions, which the committed debug keystore signs with no secret
confirm the signup screen's Skip path reaches local-only mode on the affected build and record that as reset evidence
author the trigger: create two notebooks and a note, link the note, reopen link notebooks in single-select mode, remove one, save, and re-read the note's notebooks
state identity and authority: a link the user removed must not survive the save
minimize the trigger and verify neighboring legal behavior: the same removal in multi-select mode persists correctly on both builds, which is the exact boundary the fix draws
prove three clean affected reproductions and three reached-observation fixed controls

selectedDefects.issueTitle: Album split into multiple smaller albums
selectedDefects.whySuitable: the library scanner keyed albums partly on release year, so one album whose tracks carried different or missing year tags was split into several albums in the UI. The fix changes the schema and the scanning helpers, with a drizzle migration. The trigger is entirely local: push a set of tagged audio files onto the AVD and let the app scan them, then read the artist screen. It is the third distinct adapter path in this target, media scanning driven from JavaScript over a native MediaStore read, and it is the only selected defect on the legacy bridge, since this revision sets newArchEnabled=false with Hermes on. That makes it the one candidate that would catch an adapter that silently assumes bridgeless
remaining: build the release variant at both revisions, which the documented debug fallback signs with no secret
author the audio fixture set: tracks of one album with differing and missing year tags, tagged deterministically and stored with the campaign
drive the initial scan and grant media permission through UiAutomator2, then read the album list on the artist screen
state identity and authority: one album's tracks must be grouped as one album
minimize the trigger and verify neighboring legal behavior: two genuinely different albums by the same artist stay separate on both builds
confirm the drizzle migration path does not require a pre-existing database, since the campaign installs onto a reset AVD
prove three clean affected reproductions and three reached-observation fixed controls
selectedDefects.executionOutcome: seeding is correct and proven: MediaStore's scan_file and scan_volume are called through the content provider, the audio volume is queried back, and all four fixtures are confirmed indexed before the application launches. The campaign stops on the application: after the media permission is granted the library still reports zero tracks for the full 300 second bound. What makes this application ingest an already-populated volume is the remaining input
